Overview -

Company Information -

Contoso, Ltd is a multinational retail company that builds, deploys, and manages generative AI and agent-based solutions by using Microsoft

Foundry.

Existing Environment -

Identity Environment -

Contoso uses Microsoft Entra ID for identity management, authentication, and authorization capabilities that enable agents to access

organizational resources and services.

Contoso recently formed a new AI engineering team named Agent1Dev Team to optimize and maintain existing AI solutions.

The team collaborates with solution architects, DevOps engineers, and security engineers to design, implement. monitor, and secure AI

applications.

Contoso also has a team named Agent1Test Team that is responsible for validating AI solutions before the solution deployments.

Generative Environment -

Contoso has a Microsoft Foundry deployment that contains two projects named Project1 and Project2.

Project1 -

Project1 contains a customer support agent named Agent1 that assists customers with product inquiries and troubleshooting requests.

Agent1 has the following configurations:

Agent1 uses a base model deployment.

A safety evaluation pipeline is NOT enabled.

Tool invocation approval workflows are NOT enabled.

Conversation memory constraints are NOT configured.

Agent1 interacts with customers by using digital support channels and answers general questions about Contoso products.

Project1 is deployed to an Azure region located in the European Union (EU).

Agent1Dev Team will use Project1 to optimize and maintain Agent1.

Project2 -

Project2 contains a deployed video generation model. The marketing department at Contoso has access to Project2 and plans to use the model to

develop a video creation solution.

Development of the solution is incomplete.

Data Environment -

Contoso stores product-related information in Azure resources that support AI applications.

The Azure environment contains an Azure Blob Storage account named storage1 that stores product detail sheets for all the Contoso products.

The product sheets include specifications, feature descriptions, and product support information that Agent1 can use to answer customer

questions. The product sheets are stored in the PDF format.

Problem Statements -

Contoso identifies the following issues:

Agent1 has only general knowledge of the Contoso products.

A recent chat interaction with Agent1 was analyzed for sentiment. The results of the analysis have NOT been processed yet.

Agent1 does NOT use the detailed product information in the product sheets stored in storage1 when responding to customer questions.

The finance department at Contoso reports that vendor invoices must be reviewed manually to ensure that the invoices match the terms defined in

the vendor contracts. The invoices contain tables, logos, and varied layouts that make the documents difficult to process consistently.

Requirements -

Planned Changes -

Contoso plans to implement the following changes:

Implement a solution for Project1 that analyzes the vendor invoices by evaluating both the visual layout and the textual content of the invoices, so

that the invoice details can be verified against the vendor contract terms.

Update the base model deployment used by Agent1 and standardize the model version to ensure continuity and consistent responses.

Enable Agent1 to retrieve and use the detailed product information from the product sheets stored in storage1.

Implement an indexing solution for the product sheets that Agent1 can use to answer customer questions.

Complete the development of the video creation solution.

Technical Requirements -

Contoso identifies the following technical requirements:

The model deployment used by Agent1 must support scalable, high-throughput generative AI workloads and dynamically scale to handle variable

customer support traffic, without requiring reserved throughput capacity.

The product sheets must be processed by using an indexing pipeline that enables semantic and vector search, so that Agent1 can retrieve the

relevant product information.

Responses generated by using the product sheet information must be relevant, complete, and accurate.

Agent1 must be able to use the product sheets to answer natural language questions about product details.

The model version used by Agent1 must remain consistent to ensure stable responses.

The data processed by the model must remain within the EU.

Security and Compliance Requirements

Contoso identifies the following security and compliance requirements:

API keys must NOT be used to access Foundry-deployed models.

Access to the Azure resources must follow the principle of least privilege.

The developers at Contoso must authenticate to Microsoft Foundry resources by using Microsoft Entra authentication.

Access to Project1 must be assigned to the members of Agent1Dev Team by using a security group named SC_Agent1_Dev.

Access to Project1 must be assigned to the members of Agent1Test Team by using a security group named SC_Agent1_Test.

Agent1 must never reveal customer information, even if a document that contains customer data is added erroneously to the product sheet

repository in storage1.

The product sheets might contain images that include embedded text. Agent1 must be protected from malicious instructions potentially hidden

within the images.

Business Requirements -

Contoso identifies the following business requirements:

Users that interact with Agent1 must have a personalized experience in future interactions, including the ability for Agent1 to retain conversation

context and recall relevant information from previous interactions.

Agent1 must answer questions only about the products sold by Contoso.

options.explanation: Standard is a pay-as-you-go deployment type that scales with request demand without reserving provisioned throughput units (PTUs). Unlike Global Standard, processing stays within the deployment's Azure geography, so it fits the EU data-residency requirement.
Global Standard can route inference traffic across supported global regions. That conflicts with the requirement that model processing remain within the EU.
Global Provisioned uses reserved provisioned throughput and can route processing globally. The scenario explicitly requires dynamic scaling without reserved throughput and requires EU data residency.
Upgrading when the current version expires still allows the deployed model version to change automatically later, so it does not guarantee a consistent version.

options.text: Opt out of automatic model version upgrades
options.explanation: Opting out of automatic model version upgrades prevents the deployment from moving to a newer model version automatically, which avoids unplanned behavior changes. The team must still migrate manually before the pinned version retires; after retirement, a NoAutoUpgrade deployment stops working rather than upgrading itself.

options.text: Upgrade once a new default version becomes available
options.explanation: This policy upgrades the deployment whenever a new default version becomes available. That can change model behavior and therefore conflicts with the requirement for a consistent model version.

communityNotes.summary: The discussion distinguishes regional Standard from Global Standard and provisioned deployments. Standard is the defensible choice because the workload must scale without reserved throughput while processing remains in the selected EU region.
caveats: Global Standard offers highly elastic throughput, but it can route inference outside the selected region.
Data Zone Standard could be relevant in a different option set, but it is not offered in this question.

question:
You are planning a Microsoft Foundry project named Project1 that will contain multiple agents. Each agent will access the same Azure AI Search

resource.

You need to recommend a solution to centrally manage the Azure AI Search credentials within Project1. The solution must be implemented across

all the agents.

What should you recommend?

options.text: Enable role-based access control (RBAC) for the Azure AI Search resource.
options.explanation: Azure RBAC controls which identities may access the Search resource and what operations they may perform. It manages authorization, not a reusable project-level connection and its credentials.

options.text: Disable key-based access control on the Azure AI Search resource.
options.explanation: Disabling key-based access forces clients to use Microsoft Entra authentication. This improves credential security but does not centrally register the Search connection for all project agents.

options.text: Add a connection to the Azure AI Search resource.
options.explanation: A project connection stores the endpoint and authentication configuration once and allows every agent in the project to reuse it. RBAC and private endpoints solve authorization and networking concerns rather than central connection management.

options.text: Create a managed private endpoint that connects to the Azure AI Search resource.
options.explanation: A managed private endpoint keeps traffic to Azure AI Search on a private network path. It solves network isolation, not central credential and connection management.

question:
Your company is piloting a customer support agent in a Microsoft Foundry project name Project1. Project1 is connected to an existing Application

Insights resource, and the company’s support team reviews runs in the Traces tab.

The Foundry Agent Service is configured to perform the following actions:

Retrieve the Application Insights connection string by calling project_client.telemetry.get_application_insights_connection_string().

Call configure_azure_monitor(connection_string=...) to enable telemetry.

A separate LangChain service is configured to use OpenTelemetry and has the following configurations:

Uses AzureAIOpenTelemetryTracer(connection_string=..., enable_content_recording=False)

Passes the tracer by using config={“callbacks”:[azure_tracer]}

Company policy has the following requirements:

Telemetry from LangChain and OpenTelemetry must be distinguishable within the same Application Insights resource.

Secrets and credentials must NOT be stored in prompts, tool arguments, or span attributes.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

rows.text: The LangChain service will appear in Traces without configuring a tracer.
rows.explanation: No. A separate LangChain service is not traced merely because the Foundry project is connected to Application Insights. LangChain must be instrumented with an OpenTelemetry-compatible tracer/callback so its spans are emitted to the same Application Insights resource.

rows.text: Setting different OTEL_SERVICE_NAME values separates the services in Application Insights.
rows.explanation: Yes. OTEL_SERVICE_NAME sets the OpenTelemetry service.name resource attribute. Giving the Foundry service and LangChain service different service names lets their telemetry be distinguished even when both export to the same Application Insights resource.

rows.text: When using enable_content_recording=False, prompts and tool data will be captured in the telemetry.
rows.explanation: No. enable_content_recording=False disables capture of sensitive prompt/message content and tool-call content in the LangChain OpenTelemetry spans. Tracing metadata can still be emitted, but the prompt and tool data themselves are not recorded.

You have a Microsoft Foundry project that processes procurement documents submitted by suppliers.

You need to implement two pipelines by using Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools. The solution must meet the following requirements:

Include a pipeline named Pipeline1 that supports cost-effective, high-volume processing of standalone PDF invoices.

Include a pipeline named Pipeline2 that supports cross-document validation by using multi-step reasoning and reference data.

How should you configure each pipeline? To answer, drag the appropriate configurations to the correct pipelines. Each configuration may be used

once, more than once, of not at all. You may need to drag the split bar between panes or scroll to view content.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

targets.explanation: Standard mode is designed for high-volume, cost-effective analysis of a single file. Pipeline1 processes standalone PDF invoices and does not require cross-document reasoning or reference data, so a single-file task in standard mode is appropriate.

Pro mode adds advanced multi-step reasoning and support for multiple files/reference data. Pipeline2 must compare information across documents and validate it against reference data, so it needs a multi-file task in pro mode.

question:
You have a Python application named App1 that integrates with a Microsoft Foundry project named Project1.

You need to ensure that App1 meets the following requirements:

Authenticates by using a Microsoft Entra managed identity

Sends prompts to a deployed model by using the Azure OpenAI Responses API

How should you complete the Python code? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: AzureKeyCredential authenticates with a static service key. It cannot satisfy the requirement to use a Microsoft Entra managed identity.
ClientSecretCredential uses a tenant ID, client ID, and stored client secret. It is an application credential, not managed identity authentication.

DefaultAzureCredential is an Azure Identity credential chain that can obtain Microsoft Entra tokens from a managed identity when the app runs on an Azure host with managed identity enabled. It avoids storing API keys or client secrets, so it meets the managed-identity requirement.
compact reduces stored conversation context so it consumes fewer tokens. It does not send the prompt and create the requested model response.

responses.create is the Responses API operation that creates a new model response from the supplied input. retrieve only fetches an already-created response, while compact reduces stored conversation context rather than sending a new prompt.
retrieve fetches a response that was created previously. It cannot create a new response from the current prompt.

answerTemplate.content:
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient

credential = {{credential}}()

project_client = AIProjectClient(
    endpoint="https://contosoai.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/project1",
    credential=credential,
)
with project_client.get_openai_client() as openai_client:
    response = openai_client.responses.{{responsesMethod}}(
        model="trail-guide-chat",
        input="Create a 3-day hiking itinerary near Seattle.",
    )
    print(response.output_text)

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains a workflow for a customer support triage process.

You have an Ask a question node that stores user responses in a local variable named Var01.

You need to create the following Power Fx expressions:

An if/else condition expression that ensures that Var01 contains a value

A Send message expression that returns the stored user response in uppercase

How should you configure the expressions? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: IsBlank(Local.Var01) is true when the local variable has no value. The workflow needs the opposite condition so it continues after the user supplied an answer.
IsEmpty is intended for an empty table or collection in Power Fx. Var01 stores one response value, so IsBlank is the appropriate test.
Not(IsBlank(Local.Var01)) is true only after the local response variable contains a value, allowing the next step to run.
{Local.Var01} inserts the response exactly as entered. It does not apply the required uppercase transformation.

`Upper()` is the Power Fx text function that converts a string to uppercase. `Local.Var01` is the correctly scoped workflow variable containing the user's response, so `{Upper(Local.Var01)}` both reads the stored answer and applies the required transformation.
{Upper(Var01)} performs uppercase conversion but omits the Local scope, so it does not reference the stored local workflow variable correctly.

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains a customer support agent built by using the Foundry Agent Service.

The agent uploads user-provided screenshots to Azure Storage through a ticketing tool and receives a blob URL for additional reasoning.

You need to use image moderation during agent runs and prevent harmful content from being returned during runs. Azure AI Content Safety must

access the images by using the blob URL. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

What should you configure for Content Safety? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Select Tool call and set Action to Block.
options.explanation: Blocking Tool call output would stop content returned by a tool. The risky data enters as user input and can appear in the model output, so this targets the wrong stages.

options.text: Select User input and Output and set Action to Annotate.
options.explanation: Annotate labels detections in user input and output but allows the content to continue. It does not enforce the required blocking action.

options.text: Select User input and Tool response and set Action to Annotate.
options.explanation: This annotates user input and tool responses without blocking them, and it monitors tool response rather than the model output required by the scenario.

options.text: Select User input, Output, Tool response, and Tool call and set Action to Block.
options.explanation: This applies blocking across user input, model output, tool responses, and tool calls, preventing detected unsafe or disallowed content from continuing at any stage.
Storage access keys are long-lived shared secrets. They violate the requirement for identity-based, keyless access.

options.text: A user-assigned identity that is assigned the Storage Queue Data Contributor role
options.explanation: This identity has Queue Data Contributor, which authorizes queue data. The tool uploads screenshots as blobs, so it needs a blob data role instead.

options.text: A system-assigned managed identity that is assigned the Storage Blob Data Reader role
options.explanation: Storage Blob Data Reader is normally the least-privilege read role for blobs, but it is not accepted by the Azure AI Content Safety blob-URL flow documented by Microsoft. For that flow, the Content Safety managed identity must have Storage Blob Data Contributor or Storage Blob Data Owner.

options.text: A system-assigned managed identity that is assigned the Storage Blob Data Contributor role
options.explanation: Azure AI Content Safety can fetch an image from a blob URL by using its system-assigned managed identity. Microsoft's blob-URL quickstart explicitly requires Storage Blob Data Contributor or Storage Blob Data Owner; Contributor is the less-privileged of those two accepted roles.

communityNotes.summary: The storage-role answer is corrected to Storage Blob Data Contributor because Microsoft's current Content Safety blobUrl flow accepts Contributor or Owner, not Reader.
caveats: This is an unusual case where the documented service requirement is broader than the permissions you might expect from a pure read operation.

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains three agents as shown in the following table.

You need to orchestrate the agents to ensure that the customer requests meet the following requirements:

Support a deterministic, step-based process that uses conditional branching and shared state across the agents.

Optionally trigger a ticket action based on the triage result.

The solution must minimize development effort.

What should you include in the solution?

rows: Answers policy questions by searching internal content
Creates or updates tickets by calling an HTTP API

options.explanation: A Foundry workflow provides deterministic steps, conditional branches, shared state, and optional actions without requiring custom orchestration code.

options.text: threads and runs without a workflow
options.explanation: Threads retain conversation state and runs execute an agent against that state. Without a workflow, they do not provide the deterministic multi-agent sequence and branching required here.
A multi-agent group chat lets agents collaborate conversationally and decide who responds. It is less deterministic than a workflow with predefined steps and conditions.

options.text: separate agent runs coordinated in the application code
options.explanation: Application code can coordinate separate agent runs, but the orchestration, state handling, and branching must then be built and maintained manually instead of using a Foundry workflow.

You fine-tune a baseline speech to text model for the en-us locale and publish the model.

The agent calls the Speech to text REST API and returns an error message indicating that the project ID is invalid.

You need to set the project property to the correct ID.

To what should you set the project property?

options.explanation: The project URL identifies where a project API is hosted. It does not identify the Custom Speech project that owns the trained model.

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains an agent named PaymentAgent.

PaymentAgent includes a function tool that issues customer refunds by using an external API.

You are creating a workflow in YAML.

You need to ensure that the workflow pauses for human approval and continues with the refund step only after approval is granted.

How should you complete the workflow definition? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: ask_question pauses the workflow and collects a human response, providing the approval checkpoint before the refund tool can run.
basic_chat runs a model conversation step. It does not pause execution and collect an explicit human approval decision.
data_transformation reshapes or maps workflow data. It cannot ask a person to approve the proposed refund.
approval == "approved" checks the human answer explicitly, so the refund tool runs only after approval.
Checking whether the proposal has output only confirms that a refund was proposed. It does not confirm that a human approved it.
A condition of true always executes the refund path and therefore bypasses the approval safeguard.

answerTemplate.content:
steps:
  - id: propose_refund
    type: agent
    agent: PaymentAgent
  - id: approval
    type: {{approvalType}}
  - id: execute_refund
    type: agent
    agent: PaymentAgent
    condition: {{condition}}

question:
You have an Azure Speech in Foundry Tools resource that hosts a custom speech to text model deployed to a custom endpoint. An agent uses the

endpoint to perform real-time speech recognition.

You are approaching the expiration date of the custom speech to text model.

What is the expected behavior when the model expires?

options.text: Speech recognition requests will return a 4xx error until a new custom model is deployed.
options.explanation: A 4xx failure is the documented behavior for some batch-transcription uses of an expired model. Real-time recognition through the custom endpoint instead falls back to the current base model for the locale.

options.text: Speech recognition requests will continue to use the expired custom model until the model is removed manually.
options.explanation: An expired model is no longer used indefinitely for real-time recognition. The custom endpoint falls back to the latest supported base model for the locale.

options.text: Speech recognition requests will fall back to the most recent base model for the same locale.
options.explanation: For real-time recognition through a custom endpoint, an expired custom model falls back to the latest base model for the same locale. The 4xx behavior applies to batch transcription.

options.text: The custom model will be deleted automatically when the model expires.
options.explanation: Expiration stops the custom model from being used, but it does not automatically delete the model resource. Deletion and expiration are separate lifecycle actions.

communityNotes.summary: A custom endpoint and batch transcription behave differently after model expiration. Real-time recognition through a custom endpoint falls back to the latest base model for the locale; batch transcription against an expired model fails with a 4xx response.

You have an application that calls the deployment by using the Azure OpenAI v1 API and DefaultAzureCredential.

The developers at your company receive HTTP 403 errors when they send inference requests, even after running az login.

You need to ensure that the developers can perform model inference. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

options.explanation: Cognitive Services User grants data-plane access to supported Azure AI services generally. Azure OpenAI inference requires the OpenAI-specific user role in this scenario.

question:

options.text: Route all the requests to a smaller model.
options.explanation: Routing every request to a smaller model reduces cost and latency, but difficult reasoning requests may lose quality because they can never escalate to a stronger model.

options.text: Use a model cascade that routes the requests to different models.
options.explanation: A model cascade sends routine requests to a smaller, faster model and escalates difficult requests to a stronger model, reducing average cost without sacrificing complex-answer quality.

options.explanation: max_tokens sets the upper limit for generated output length. Increasing it can raise cost and latency and does not route simple and complex requests to different models.

options.text: Route all the requests to the most capable model.
options.explanation: Routing every request to the most capable model protects quality but keeps cost and latency high for simple FAQ requests.

Periodic HTTP 429 rate limit exceeded errors during peak hours

options.text: Model Availability Rate and Provisioned Utilization
options.explanation: Model Availability Rate reveals service availability, while Provisioned Utilization reveals whether capacity is saturated. Together they address missing answers and 429 throttling.

options.explanation: Counting only HTTP 200 requests shows successful volume but hides failed and throttled requests, so it cannot diagnose the reported issues.

options.explanation: Time to Response and Total Tokens explain latency and consumption. They do not directly show model availability or provisioned-capacity saturation.

You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains an agent.

The agent uses tools to retrieve internal content and call external APIs. The agent is configured to let the model decide when to call the tools.

You need to publish the agent for a compliance workflow. The solution must meet the following requirements:

Each workflow run must include a retrieval step before generating a response.

Tool calls must authenticate by using the published agent’s own identity.

Tool access must use an identity isolated from other project resources.

Tool access must use support audit tracing.

What should you do? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: auto lets the model decide whether a tool is necessary. The agent can therefore still answer without calling one.
`none` disables tool invocation for the run, so the model must answer without retrieval or other tools. That directly violates the requirement that every workflow run include a retrieval step.

tool_choice="required" prevents the model from completing the run without calling at least one tool. options.explanation: Putting API keys in prompts exposes credentials to the model, logs, and potentially users. It is neither secure nor an identity-based authentication method.

options.text: Using the shared project agent identity
options.explanation: A shared project identity makes separate client applications act as the same principal. It cannot provide the required per-application isolation and auditing.

options.text: Using a distinct agent identity bound to the client application
options.explanation: A distinct agent identity bound to the published client application isolates tool permissions from shared project identities. It provides identity-based, auditable access for the published agent without putting API keys or other credentials in prompts or tool arguments.

A key-phrase extraction model returns important words or phrases from text. It cannot conduct a support conversation or generate grounded answers.
An LLM is designed for long-context natural-language generation and multi-step reasoning. An SLM prioritizes efficiency, while multimodal and key-phrase models solve different tasks.

options.explanation: Temperature controls sampling randomness. Temperature 2 produces highly varied output. It makes deterministic regression comparison even less reliable.

You are creating an image-editing workflow in a Microsoft Foundry project.

Ensure that background objects can be removed by applying a mask-based inpainting edit.

How should you configure the workflow?

options.text: Set generation mode to image_variation and provide the original image as a reference.
options.explanation: Image variation creates an alternative derived from the reference image and can change the entire composition. It does not confine editing to the background region that must be removed.

options.text: Enable text_to_image mode and a prompt describing the desired background removal.
options.explanation: Text-to-image creates a new image from a prompt. It does not edit only a specified region of the existing image or guarantee preservation of its lighting and style.

options.text: Enable image_to_image mode and a high-strength value to regenerate the full image based on the prompt.
options.explanation: High-strength image-to-image regeneration allows broad changes across the entire image. It does not protect the unmasked pixels that must remain unchanged.

options.text: Enable mask_inpainting and supply both the input image and a mask indicating which part of the image to modify.
options.explanation: The option describes the correct mask-based editing concept: the mask identifies the region that may change while the surrounding image is retained. In the current API this is an image-edit request with an input image and mask; `mask_inpainting` is not the documented mode name.

communityNotes.summary: Mask-based image editing is verified, but the current API expresses this as an image-edit request with an input image plus a mask rather than a `mask_inpainting` mode.

options.text: Apply a mask-based inpainting edit to the part of the image that contains the logo.
options.explanation: Inpainting with a mask targets the logo region specifically. Guidance, seed, and prompt changes regenerate broader parts of the image.

options.text: Modify the original prompt to exclude brand names.
options.explanation: A negative prompt can discourage logos in a newly generated image, but it does not reliably remove a logo from an already approved image while preserving everything else.

options.text: Rerun the prompt by using a different random seed.
options.explanation: Changing the random seed generates a different overall variation. It may remove the logo by chance but can also alter unrelated parts of the image.

Which built-in analyzer should you use?

options.explanation: A document field schema defines fields to extract into structured output. By itself it is not the prebuilt analyzer that preserves tables, layout, and QR-code information.

OCR or the prebuilt-read analyzer extracts printed and handwritten text, but does not preserve the full document structure needed for layout-aware processing. The prebuilt-layout analyzer extracts text together with structural elements such as tables, selection marks, and document layout.
Document search is intended to make document content retrievable. It is not the layout-analysis model used to extract structural elements from the PDF.
The prebuilt-layout model extracts structural elements such as tables and can detect barcodes and QR codes; prebuilt-read focuses on OCR text.

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains an agent.

The agent accepts user-uploaded screenshots and uses a multimodal chat model.

Some screenshots contain potentially malicious embedded text.

You need to prevent a prompt injection attack and ensure that third-party content is treated as lower trust.

How should you configure prompt shields for document attacks? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: Disabling Prompt Shields turns off detection of direct or indirect prompt-injection attacks at that guardrail stage. Because the requirement is specifically to stop malicious instructions in retrieved content, disabling the protection cannot meet the goal.

Block stops content when Prompt Shields detects a disallowed indirect prompt-injection attack. Annotate only records the detection and allows processing to continue, so Block is required when malicious instructions must not reach the model.
Annotate records the detected injection but still sends the content through the workflow. The requirement is to stop it.

Spotlighting marks untrusted document content so the model can distinguish it from trusted instructions and is a documented mitigation for indirect prompt injection. However, Microsoft's current Foundry guardrails documentation says Spotlighting is not yet applicable to agents, so this option cannot currently satisfy the scenario as written.
A blocklist catches only known terms or patterns. Hidden image instructions can use unlimited wording, so semantic prompt-injection protection is needed.

options.text: Use optical character recognition (OCR) to extract the text from the images first.
options.explanation: OCR can expose text embedded in screenshot pixels so text-based prompt-injection controls can inspect it, but OCR by itself is only extraction; it does not classify or neutralize malicious instructions.

communityNotes.summary: Prompt Shields can detect indirect attacks, but the second intended mitigation is currently incompatible with the scenario: Spotlighting is supported for models but not yet for Foundry agents.
caveats: Keep the historical/intended answer only as a study caveat; the current Microsoft guardrails table marks Spotlighting as not applicable to agents.

You need to automatically classify uploaded images for harmful content. The solution must block content based on severity levels.

What should you do?

options.explanation: OCR extracts machine-readable text from pixels. Keyword scanning can then match literal words in that OCR output, but it cannot classify the visual image itself into harm categories or apply severity-based moderation to the photo.
Prompt Shields detect prompt-injection attempts that try to override model instructions. They are a security control for adversarial prompts, not a visual-harm classifier for uploaded images.

A custom blocklist matches explicitly configured words or phrases. It is useful for known textual terms, but it cannot semantically classify arbitrary harmful visual content or assign image severity levels.

Image moderation analyzes the visual content of an uploaded image, classifies supported harm categories, and returns severity information that can be used to block images above configured thresholds. That directly matches the requirement.

options.explanation: Image moderation classifies harmful visual content such as violence or sexual content. The problem here is not visual harm; it is malicious instructions contained in OCR-extracted text, so image moderation addresses a different risk.

Prompt Shields for Documents inspect third-party or retrieved text for indirect prompt-injection instructions. Because the OCR result is appended as untrusted contextual text, the document shield is the control that targets the stated attack.
Protected-material detection looks for likely reproduction of copyrighted or otherwise protected text/code. It does not determine whether OCR text is trying to manipulate the model's instructions.

The agent must receive continuous audio input, convert the input into text for reasoning, and then return spoken responses to a user. The

workflow must meet the following requirements:

Support turn-taking dynamics, where the agent begins to generate the speech output before the user finishes speaking.

options.text: Use batch transcription to convert the audio input and return text responses from the agent.
options.explanation: Batch transcription processes completed or uploaded recordings asynchronously. It is not designed to stream partial recognition results during a live conversation, and returning text-only responses also fails the spoken-output requirement.

options.text: Use real-time speech to text for incoming audio and text to speech for agent responses.
options.explanation: A conversational voice agent needs streaming speech recognition for input and text-to-speech synthesis for output; embeddings and translation do not provide that turn-taking loop.

options.text: Use an embeddings model to encode the audio, and then decode the audio into text and speech.
options.explanation: Audio embeddings represent acoustic content numerically for comparison or downstream models. They are not reversible speech-to-text and text-to-speech conversion steps.

options.text: Use speech translation to convert the audio into another language and return the translated text.
options.explanation: Speech translation recognizes speech and translates it to a target language. The scenario requires same-workflow conversational recognition plus spoken responses, not translation to another language, so speech translation does not provide the required input/output loop.

It is not the project-scoped identity used when an in-development agent/tool is configured for project-managed-identity authentication to a downstream service.

options.text: Enable a system-assigned managed identity at the project level
options.explanation: A project-level managed identity provides keyless Microsoft Entra authentication for project-scoped service-to-service tool access. When the agent uses project-managed-identity authentication, grant only the downstream permissions that identity needs.

options.text: Create a service principal and store the principal's client secret.
options.explanation: A service principal authenticated with a client secret still requires storing and rotating a secret, so it does not meet the keyless-credentials requirement. A managed identity removes that stored credential.

options.explanation: A Key Vault access policy can grant secret read permissions when the vault is configured to use the legacy access-policy authorization model. options.text: Assign the Key Vault Secrets User role to the managed identity.
options.explanation: Key Vault Secrets User is a data-plane RBAC role that can read secret contents without granting secret management or vault administration. For direct secret retrieval by the project identity, it is the least-privilege role among these options.

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains an agent. The agent uses threads and file uploads and calls an Azure OpenAI model

deployment.

file size exceeded error.

Use additional agent tools to reduce the message size.
Implement exponential backoff and jitter in the retry logic.

targets.correctAnswer: Implement exponential backoff and jitter in the retry logic.
targets.explanation: HTTP 429 means the request was throttled because a rate or quota limit was reached. Exponential backoff increases the delay between retries and jitter randomizes retry timing so many clients do not retry simultaneously; honor Retry-After when provided.

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project.

You need to create a customer support agent that meets the following requirements:

• Grounds responses only in company policy documents stored in curated repositories

• Retains customer preferences across separate chat sessions

How should you configure the agent? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Configure retrieval from approved data sources.
options.explanation: Retrieval from approved sources keeps policy documents in curated repositories and supplies only retrieved evidence to the agent.

options.text: Upload the policy documents direct to the agent.
options.explanation: Direct uploads create agent-managed files and bypass the requirement that policies remain in the approved curated repositories.

options.text: Embed the policy documents directly into the agent instructions.
options.explanation: Embedding full documents in instructions consumes context, is difficult to update, and bypasses controlled retrieval from the authoritative repositories.
Orchestration-managed session context retains temporary state during a session. It does not provide durable preference recall across separate conversations.

options.text: Enable agent memory that uses persistent storage.
options.explanation: Persistent agent memory stores user-specific information, such as preferences, and makes relevant memories retrievable in later conversations. That cross-session persistence is exactly what the requirement asks for; grounding sources alone do not retain per-user preferences.

options.text: Retain user preferences in the state of the client application.
options.explanation: Client-side state can retain preferences on one device or app instance, but it is not centralized agent memory and may not follow the user across clients.

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains an agent. The agent generates summaries from retrieved policy documents.

You need to improve response completeness. The solution must be implemented in the logic of the application code before responses are

returned.

What should you do?

options.text: Add a retry evaluation before the responses are returned.
options.explanation: A retry evaluation checks the draft for required content before returning it and regenerates when the completeness condition fails.

options.text: Decrease the value of the temperature parameter.
options.explanation: Lower temperature makes output more deterministic, but it does not inspect whether required clauses are present or trigger regeneration when they are missing.

options.text: Increase the value of the presence_penalty parameter
options.explanation: Presence penalty discourages the model from repeating tokens or topics already present. It does not enforce inclusion of required regulatory clauses.

options.text: Replace the model with a smaller deployment.
options.explanation: A smaller model can reduce cost and latency but may have lower reasoning capacity. It does not add the required completeness validation loop.

subcategory: Design and implement multimodal understanding workflows
question:
You develop a test method to verify the results retrieved from a call to the Azure Vision in Foundry Tools API. The call is used to analyze the

existence of company logos in images. The call returns a collection of brands named brands.

You have the following code segment:

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

rows.text: The code will display the name of each detected brand with a confidence equal to or higher than 75 percent.
rows.explanation: Yes. The condition brand.confidence >= 0.75 means the print statement runs only for detected brands whose confidence score is at least 0.75, which is 75%.

rows.text: The code will display coordinates for the top-left corner of the rectangle that contains the brand logo of the displayed brands.
rows.explanation: Yes. In the Vision brand rectangle, x and y identify the rectangle's top-left origin. The code prints rectangle.x and rectangle.y, so those are the top-left coordinates.

rows.text: The code will display coordinates for the bottom-right corner of the rectangle that contains the brand logo of the displayed brands.
rows.explanation: No. rectangle.w and rectangle.h are width and height, not the bottom-right x/y coordinates. The bottom-right point would be calculated as (x + w, y + h).

category: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
subcategory: Set up AI solutions in Foundry
question:
You have an Azure subscription.

You plan to build an app that will use the Azure AI DALL-E model.

You need to deploy the model.

What should you use?

options.text: the Azure SDK for Python and PowerShell cmdlets.
options.explanation: Azure SDKs and PowerShell can automate supported Azure resources, but they do not make a retired model deployable. DALL-E 3 was retired in Azure on March 4, 2026, so no current deployment method can create a new DALL-E 3 deployment.

options.text: the Azure SDK for JavaScript and Azure Machine Learning Studio.
options.explanation: Azure Machine Learning Studio is not the current deployment surface for Azure OpenAI image models in this scenario. More importantly, DALL-E 3 is retired and no longer available for new deployments.

options.text: Microsoft Foundry and the Azure Command Line Interface (CLI)
options.explanation: Historically, Microsoft Foundry and Azure CLI could be used in a DALL-E deployment workflow. However, Microsoft retired `dall-e-3` on March 4, 2026; new deployments are unavailable and existing deployments are non-functional. Current image-generation solutions should use a `gpt-image-` series model instead.

options.text: the Azure portal and Microsoft Graph API
options.explanation: Microsoft Graph is for Microsoft 365/directory APIs, not Foundry model deployment. The Azure portal also cannot create a new deployment of a model that Microsoft has retired.

communityNotes.summary: This item is obsolete as a current deployment question. DALL-E 3 was retired in Azure on March 4, 2026; new deployments are unavailable and existing deployments are non-functional.
caveats: The historical/intended answer was Microsoft Foundry + Azure CLI, but there is no valid current deployment method for DALL-E 3. Microsoft directs new image-generation workloads to the GPT-image series.

category: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
subcategory: Manage, monitor, and secure AI systems
question:
You have an Azure subscription.

You need to create a new resource that will generate fictional stores in response to user prompts. The solution must ensure that the resource uses

a customer-managed key to protect data.

How should you complete the script? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: `AIServices` creates the broader Microsoft Foundry resource kind, which can also expose Azure OpenAI model capabilities together with other Foundry Tools. It is therefore technically capable of generative workloads; `OpenAI` is only uniquely preferable if the question specifically intends a standalone Azure OpenAI resource.
LanguageAuthoring is used for authoring Azure Language projects such as classification or NER. It does not host the required generative model.

`OpenAI` creates a standalone Azure OpenAI resource, which can host generative models for prompt-to-text workloads and supports customer-managed encryption. This is the intended answer if the requirement is specifically to create an Azure OpenAI resource rather than the broader `AIServices` Foundry resource.
`--api-properties` sets service-specific account properties. It does not accept the customer-managed encryption object containing `keySource` and `keyVaultProperties`.

`--assign-identity` enables a managed identity on the Cognitive Services/OpenAI resource. That identity is needed for Key Vault access, but this switch does not take the encryption JSON shown in the next line.

`--encryption` accepts the customer-managed-key configuration containing `keySource: Microsoft.KeyVault` and `keyVaultProperties`. Microsoft’s CLI example enables the managed identity with `--assign-identity` and then supplies the Key Vault encryption configuration with `--encryption`.

communityNotes.summary: `--encryption` is the parameter that accepts the customer-managed-key JSON; `--assign-identity` separately enables the resource identity used to access Key Vault.
caveats: The PDF command template omits `--assign-identity`. It is intentionally preserved to match the source; a complete current command also needs a managed identity for Key Vault access.
The `OpenAI` kind remains the intended standalone Azure OpenAI answer. The broader `AIServices` resource can also expose model capabilities, so the resource-kind wording is architecture-sensitive.

question:
You have a Python application collects customer comments before posting them to a public forum.

You need to send a text comment to Azure AI Content Safety and return the self-harm severity from the response.

How should you complete the code? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: categories expects content-safety category values, not the comment text. The comment must be passed through the text property.
text expects the comment string in this SDK request model, not a one-item list.

`AnalyzeTextOptions(text=comment)` creates the Content Safety request object and places the user's comment in its `text` field. The service analyzes the text contained in that field; the other choices do not construct the request in the format expected by `analyze_text`.
TextCategory.SELF_HARM identifies the result category; it is not a request constructor and cannot accept the comment as a function argument.
analyze_image expects image content and returns visual safety categories. The input here is a text comment.
analyze_text sends the text request to Content Safety and returns category severities including self-harm.
moderate_text is not the method exposed by the shown Content Safety SDK client; the operation is named analyze_text.
A low-level path/post call is used with a generic REST pipeline, not the typed SDK client shown in the code.

category: Implement text analysis solutions
subcategory: Apply language model text analysis
question:
You have a custom named entity recognition (NER) project in Azure Language in Foundry Tools for support tickets. The schema for the project

contains an entity type named ContactInfo.

In tagged training files, ContactInfo is used for phone numbers, email addresses, and social media handles.

Model evaluation shows low precision for ContactInfo, including false positives in which nearby text is extracted as ContactInfo.

You need to improve the precision of the project.

What should you do before retraining the model?

options.text: Lower the confidence threshold for ContactInfo.
options.explanation: Lowering the confidence threshold returns more ContactInfo predictions, including more false positives. It does not teach the model to distinguish phone numbers, email addresses, and social-media identifiers.
Auto-labeling proposes labels based on the current model. If the schema combines several distinct concepts, it can reproduce that ambiguity instead of fixing it.

options.text: Add more support tickets as training data and label more ContactInfo entities.
options.explanation: Adding more examples can improve a model when the schema is appropriate, but it does not resolve the fact that one broad ContactInfo label combines three meaningfully different entities.

options.text: Replace ContactInfo by using Phone, Email, and SocialMedia entities. Relabel every matching span.
options.explanation: Separate Phone, Email, and SocialMedia entity types give the model distinct labels and require the training spans to be relabeled accordingly.

category: Implement text analysis solutions
subcategory: Implement speech solutions
question:
You are building a text-to-speech solution that uses Azure Speech in Foundry Tools to read instructions from the script in a text file.

You discover that the solution often pronounces technical terms incorrectly.

You need to prevent the incorrect pronunciations. The solution must minimize development effort.

What should you do?

options.text: From Speech Studio, train a custom neural voice
options.explanation: Custom Neural Voice creates a synthetic voice with a particular speaker identity. It does not primarily control pronunciation of technical terms in an existing text-to-speech voice.

options.text: Use Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) to specify phonemes.
options.explanation: SSML phoneme elements specify the exact pronunciation of technical terms using a phonetic alphabet, directly correcting pronunciation.

options.text: Use Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) to apply say as rules.
options.explanation: SSML say-as controls how text such as dates, numbers, characters, or telephone numbers is interpreted. It is less precise than phonemes for specialized terminology.

options.text: Use Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) to adjust the prosody of the voice.
options.explanation: SSML prosody changes pitch, speaking rate, volume, or contour. It changes delivery but not the phonetic pronunciation of a technical term.

options.text: From Azure OpenAI use the Whisper model.
options.explanation: Whisper is a speech-to-text model that transcribes audio. It does not synthesize speech or correct text-to-speech pronunciation.

question:
You have a Python application that redacts sensitive information before sending prompt text to a language model. The application has the

following code:

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

rows.text: For sample_text, audit will include entity records for Contact and SSN.
rows.explanation: No. The request restricts piiCategories to "Person" and "PhoneNumber". The entities/audit output therefore contains matches for those requested categories; it does not add separate Contact or SSN records that were not requested.

rows.text: For sample_text, text_for_model will include john.doe@contoso.com and 859-98-0987.
rows.explanation: Yes. Because Email and SSN are not included in piiCategories, those values are not selected for redaction by this request and remain in redactedText.

rows.text: For sample_text, text_for_model will contain entity type masks for John Doe and 312-555-1234.
rows.explanation: Yes. The entityMask redaction policy replaces detected PII with masks based on entity type. John Doe is detected as Person and 312-555-1234 as PhoneNumber, so both are replaced by entity-type masks.

question:
You are developing an application that will detect faulty components produced on a factory production line. The components are specific to your

business.

You need to use the Azure Custom Vision API to help detect common faults.

Which three actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and

arrange them in the correct order.

targets.explanation: First create an object-detection project. The project defines the Custom Vision task/domain and provides the container in which images, tags, iterations, and trained models are managed.
Next upload representative images and tag the faulty components, including bounding boxes for object detection. These labeled examples are the supervised training data the model learns from.
Finally train the object-detection model. Training uses the uploaded, tagged bounding-box examples to produce a model iteration that can locate and classify faults in new images.

category: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
subcategory: Implement responsible AI across generative AI and agentic systems
question:
You are developing a new sales system that will process user-generated video and text from a public-facing website.

You plan to notify users that their data has been processed by the sales system.

Which responsible AI principle does this help meet?

options.explanation: Fairness concerns equitable treatment and avoiding systematic performance differences across groups. Informing users that their data is processed is not primarily a fairness control.
Transparency requires communicating how and when an AI system is used, including notifying users that their submitted data is being processed.
Inclusiveness focuses on designing systems that empower people with different abilities and backgrounds. User notification is more directly an issue of transparency.
Reliability and safety concern consistent operation, robustness, and harm prevention. A processing notice explains system use rather than improving technical reliability.

subcategory: Apply language model text analysis
question:
You are designing a content management system.

You need to ensure that the reading experience is optimized for users who have reduced comprehension and learning differences, such as

dyslexia. The solution must minimize development effort.

Which Azure service should you include in the solution?

options.text: Azure Document Intelligence in Foundry Tools
options.explanation: Document Intelligence extracts text, layout, tables, and fields from documents. It does not provide an accessible reading interface for users with comprehension difficulties.
Azure Language analyzes text for capabilities such as sentiment, entities, and summarization. It does not provide the complete low-effort reading-assistance experience requested.
Immersive Reader provides reading aids such as text spacing, line focus, syllables, picture dictionary, and read-aloud, directly supporting users with dyslexia and comprehension differences.
Azure Translator converts text between languages. Translation can improve language access but does not supply the broader reading and dyslexia assistance features required here.

question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure App Service app named App1.

You provision a Microsoft Foundry Service resource named CSAccount1.

You need to configure App1 to access CSAccount1. The solution must minimize administrative effort.

What should you use to configure App1?

options.text: the endpoint URI and subscription key
options.explanation: The endpoint URI identifies the Foundry resource and the subscription key authenticates an application request using key-based access. This is the direct configuration represented by this option.

options.text: the endpoint URI and an OAuth token
options.explanation: An OAuth token can authorize a request when obtained for the correct Azure resource and identity. It is short-lived and must be acquired through Microsoft Entra rather than configured as the static credential described here.

options.text: the endpoint URI and a shared access signature (SAS) token
options.explanation: A SAS token grants scoped access to services such as Storage. Microsoft Foundry Service endpoints do not use Storage-style SAS tokens for this access pattern.

options.text: a system assigned managed identity and an X.509 certificate
options.explanation: A system-assigned managed identity enables keyless Microsoft Entra authentication. An X.509 certificate is not paired with that identity for normal managed-identity access.

category: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
subcategory: Manage, monitor, and secure AI systems
question:
You have a web app that uses Azure AI Search.

When reviewing activity you see greater than expected search query volumes. You suspect that the query key is compromised.

You need to prevent unauthorized access to the search endpoint and ensure that users only have read only access to the documents collection.

The solution must minimize app downtime.

Which three actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and

arrange them in the correct order.

choices.text: Change the app to use the secondary admin key
Change the app to use the new key

targets.explanation: Create a new query key first. Azure AI Search allows multiple query keys, and query keys grant read-only document-query access, so the application can receive a replacement credential without switching to an admin key.

targets.correctAnswer: Change the app to use the new key
targets.explanation: Update the application to use the new query key while both query keys are still valid. This preserves availability during the credential cutover and keeps the app on read-only query access.

After the application is confirmed to use the replacement key, delete the compromised query key. Query keys can be deleted rather than regenerated; deleting the old key removes its access without interrupting the app now using the new key.

communityNotes.summary: Correct sequence: create a replacement query key, switch the app to it, then delete the compromised query key. Query keys are read-only and multiple query keys can coexist during the cutover.

question:
You need to create a new resource that will be used to perform sentiment analysis and optical character recognition (OCR). The solution must

meet the following requirements:

• Use a single key and endpoint to access multiple services.

• Consolidate billing for future services that you might use.

• Support the use of Azure Vision in Foundry Tools in the future.

How should you complete the HTTP request to create the new resource? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: PATCH partially updates an existing resource. It is not the ARM method used to create or fully replace the resource at the target URI.
POST invokes actions or creates child operations where defined. ARM resource creation at a known resource ID uses PUT.
PUT creates or replaces an Azure Resource Manager resource at the specified resource URI.

`CognitiveServices` is the legacy Azure AI multi-service account kind. It provides one multi-service account that can be used across capabilities such as language sentiment analysis and vision/OCR, matching the option set in this question. Microsoft now recommends the newer `AIServices`/Foundry resource for new solutions, but `CognitiveServices` continues to work.
`ComputerVision` creates a Vision-specific resource. It cannot also provide sentiment analysis through the same multi-service account.
`TextAnalytics` creates a Language-specific resource. It cannot also provide OCR/vision through the same account.

communityNotes.summary: Strict review restores `CognitiveServices` because that is the valid legacy multi-service kind present in the offered choices. `AIServices` is the newer recommended Foundry resource kind, not an answer option here.
caveats: Treat this as a legacy-terminology item; new Foundry deployments generally use the newer `AIServices` resource model.

category: Implement computer vision solutions
subcategory: Design and implement multimodal understanding workflows
question:
You are building a model to detect objects in images.

The performance of the model based on training data is shown in the following exhibit.

Use the drop-down menus to select the answer choice that completes each statement based on the information presented in the graphic.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

interactions.prompt: The percentage of false positives is

options.explanation: The chart shows 100% precision. Precision = TP/(TP+FP), so with detected true positives and perfect precision there are 0 false positives.
25% is the chart's recall value. Recall measures the share of actual objects that were detected, `TP / (TP + FN)`; it is not the false-positive percentage.
30% is the configured overlap/IoU threshold used when deciding whether a predicted box matches a ground-truth object. It is an evaluation setting, not the percentage of false-positive detections.
50% is the probability/confidence threshold used to decide which predictions count as detections. It is a model-evaluation threshold, not the false-positive percentage.
One hundred is the precision percentage. Perfect precision implies zero false positives; it does not mean 100 false positives.

interactions.prompt: The value for the number of true positives divided by the total number of true positives and false negatives is

options.explanation: Recall is not zero because the chart shows that 25% of the actual objects were detected.
Recall is `TP / (TP + FN)`: the proportion of actual positive objects that the model successfully detects. The exhibit reports recall as 25%, so 25 is the required value.
30% is the overlap/IoU threshold used to match predicted boxes to ground truth. It affects how detections are evaluated but is not itself recall, which is `TP / (TP + FN)`.
50% is the probability/confidence threshold for including predictions. It controls which detections are considered, whereas recall is the measured `TP / (TP + FN)` value.
100% is the precision shown in the exhibit. Precision is `TP / (TP + FP)` and measures how many predicted positives are correct; recall instead measures how many actual positives were found.

media.alt: Custom Vision model performance showing precision, recall, and mAP.

communityNotes.summary: The included exhibit shows Precision 100.0%, Recall 25.0%, and mAP 77.2%. Therefore zero false positives and 25% recall are supported by the image.

category: Implement information extraction solutions
subcategory: Build retrieval and grounding pipelines
question:
You are developing an application that will use Azure AI Search for internal documents.

You need to implement document-level filtering for Azure AI Search.

Which three actions should you include in the solution? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Add allowed groups to each index entry
options.explanation: Storing allowed group IDs on each document creates the security metadata needed for document-level filtering.
Creating one index per group physically separates data but duplicates indexes, complicates ingestion, and is unnecessary for document-level security trimming.

options.text: Send access tokens from Microsoft Entra ID, with the search request.
options.explanation: Sending the user's access token authenticates the caller to Search, but Search does not automatically infer document filters from that token in the standard security-trimming pattern.
Retrieving every group in the directory is unnecessary and expensive. The application only needs the current user's group memberships.

options.text: Retrieve the group memberships of the user
options.explanation: Retrieving the current user's group memberships provides the values that can be matched against each document's allowed-groups field.

options.text: Supply the groups as a filter for the search requests
options.explanation: Supplying those group IDs as a Search filter restricts results to documents the user is allowed to access.

question:
You have an Azure AI Search indexer that ingest PDF policy manuals.

Client applications must display page-level citations that have bounding polygons for both text and images.

You need to add a single built-in multimodal content extraction skill to the Azure AI Search skillset. The solution must meet the following

requirements:

• Provide text and image location metadata.

• Extract tables that span multiple pages.

What should you add?

options.explanation: Document Layout extracts page structure and text layout. It does not provide the single multimodal extraction output required for bounding polygons covering both text and images.
Document Extraction focuses on extracting document content or fields. The required Search pipeline needs multimodal extraction that also represents image regions for citations.
Azure Content Understanding produces multimodal document representations with source grounding for text and visual regions, supporting the requested page-level citations and polygons.
GenAI Prompt generates new enriched values from supplied content. It does not perform the underlying multimodal page extraction and location mapping.

category: Implement information extraction solutions
subcategory: Build retrieval and grounding pipelines
question:
You are creating an enrichment pipeline that will use Azure AI Search. The knowledge store contains unstructured JSON data and the text from

scanned PDF documents.

Which projection type should you use for each data type? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: File projection writes binary or file-like enrichment outputs to blob storage. Unstructured JSON is better preserved as an object.
Object projection stores a hierarchical JSON object and preserves the structure of unstructured enrichment data.
Table projection flattens data into rows and columns in Azure Table Storage. It is not the best match for preserving arbitrary nested JSON.

File projections are not a general-purpose way to write text files. In an Azure AI Search knowledge store, file projections are specifically for binary normalized images from /document/normalized_images/*, so extracted OCR text does not belong in a file projection.

Object projections write enrichment output as JSON blobs in Azure Storage. Extracted OCR text can be shaped into an object with related metadata, making Object projection the valid non-tabular projection among these choices.

Table projections store shaped enrichment output as rows and columns in Azure Table Storage. They are appropriate when the downstream representation is tabular, not for unstructured extracted document text.

communityNotes.summary: Extracted OCR text should use an object projection, not a file projection. Microsoft documents knowledge-store file projections as binary normalized images; object projections store JSON blobs.

category: Implement computer vision solutions
subcategory: Create custom vision models
question:
You are building a Custom Vision model that will be deployed as part of an iOS app. You have images of cats and dogs, and each image contains either a cat or a dog.

How should you configure the project?

options.explanation: Classification assigns a category to the complete image, which is the requirement here.
Object detection locates one or more objects with bounding boxes. The question only asks which single class describes the whole image.
Each image contains exactly one of the mutually exclusive classes: cat or dog.
Multilabel is intended for images that can have more than one tag at the same time.
The Adult domain is for adult-content classification, not general animal classification or mobile export.
The Food domain is specialized for food images and is not exportable unless its compact variant is selected.
The standard General domain is suitable for broad image classification but cannot be exported for local mobile use.
Compact domains can be exported, including to CoreML for an iOS app. General (compact) fits cats and dogs.
The Landmarks domain is specialized for landmarks and the non-compact variant is not the correct mobile-export choice.
This is exportable but specialized for landmarks rather than cats and dogs.
The Retail domain is intended for retail products and the non-compact variant cannot be exported.
This is exportable but specialized for retail products rather than general animal images.

A Microsoft Foundry agent has an MCP tool named kbsearch that queries an Azure AI Search knowledge base. Some runs answer from the base model without invoking kbsearch, so the responses lack grounded citations.

You need to deterministically force the agent to invoke a tool on each run. What should you do?

options.text: Add the response_format parameter to create_and_process().
options.explanation: response_format controls the structure of the model response; it does not require a tool call.
Changing the helper method does not change the model's tool-selection policy.

options.text: Add the toolset parameter to create_and_process().
options.explanation: A toolset makes tools available, but availability alone still lets the model choose not to call one.

subcategory: Extract entities and key information from text
question:
You call get_key_words() with the text:

Our tour of London included a visit to Buckingham Palace

What will the function output?

options.explanation: Named entity recognition identifies London as a location and Buckingham Palace as a named place. Generic words such as tour and visit are not named entities.
These are ordinary nouns/actions, not the named entities identified by recognize_entities().
The loop prints each detected entity, not the complete document.
London is an entity, but Tour is not; Buckingham Palace is the other named entity.

category: Implement text analysis solutions
subcategory: Link entities to knowledge bases
question: The following code calls linked entity recognition for a document. For each statement, select Yes if it is true; otherwise, select No.

supportingContent.content:
from azure.core.credentials import AzureKeyCredential
from azure.ai.textanalytics import TextAnalyticsClient

text_analytics_client = TextAnalyticsClient(
    endpoint=endpoint,
    credential=AzureKeyCredential(key)
)
documents = [
    "Our tour guide took us up the Space Needle during our trip to Seattle last week."
]
result = text_analytics_client.recognize_linked_entities(documents)

rows.text: The code will detect the language of the documents.
rows.explanation: No. recognize_linked_entities performs entity linking. Language detection requires a separate detect_language call.

rows.text: The url attribute returned for each linked entity will be a Bing search link.
rows.explanation: No. url is the URL of the identified knowledge-base entry, commonly a Wikipedia page, not a Bing search-results link.

rows.text: The matches attribute returned for each linked entity will provide the location in a document where the entity is referenced.
rows.explanation: Yes. Each match includes offset and length information that identifies where the entity mention occurs in the document.

category: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
subcategory: Select and deploy models
question: A Microsoft Foundry support-ticket app must compare candidate models by quality, cost, and throughput, and must avoid hosting model weights in your Azure subscription. What should you configure?

options.explanation: Private endpoints control network access; they do not compare models by quality, cost, and throughput.

options.text: Use deployment lists and license tabs
options.explanation: Deployment and licensing details do not provide the requested comparative benchmark view.

options.text: Use tool catalog connections and run traces
options.explanation: Tools and traces help inspect agent execution, not compare candidate foundation models.

options.text: Use model catalog leaderboards and model cards
options.explanation: Leaderboards provide comparative benchmark results, while model cards describe capabilities, costs, and deployment characteristics.
Bringing your own model normally requires you to host and operate the model weights.
A vector index stores embeddings for retrieval; it is not a model deployment option.
Serverless API deployment lets the provider host and operate the model instead of placing model weights in your subscription.
Managed compute deploys the model to compute in your subscription and therefore hosts the model there.

category: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
subcategory: Use embeddings and vector representations
question: You need to compare documents for semantic similarity. The solution must return numeric vectors that represent the tokens of each document and minimize development effort. Which Azure OpenAI model type should you use?
